title: finding(components): element:text / button / image / number apply `aria.ariaLabel` as `aria-arialabel`, so the declared accessible name never reaches the DOM
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a product defect with a named site, class (a). `reach:` public door, measured once (below). Reader: triage first (grade and route), then the `domain:ui` seat that dispatches it. Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`) from the objectui#10993 batch-1 dev report (PR objectui#11050, `out_of_scope_findings`), re-read at source before filing. ⛔ Not graded here.

## The site

`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx`, the file-local helper `ariaAttrs`, read at objectui `origin/main` `bf7ab35ce`:

```ts
out[k.startsWith('aria-') || k === 'role' ? k : `aria-${k}`] = String(v);
```

The spec's `AriaProps` spells the accessible name `ariaLabel` (and `ariaDescribedBy`). The helper prefixes the key as written, so `aria: { ariaLabel: 'Order total' }` becomes the attribute `aria-ariaLabel`, which the DOM lowercases to `aria-arialabel`: an attribute no assistive technology reads. The node never gets an `aria-label`. The helper is spread by `element:text`, `element:button`, `element:image` and `element:number` (six `ariaAttrs(` call sites in the file).

A per-locale map on `ariaLabel` (the spec types it `I18nLabel`) is also stringified raw, to `[object Object]`. That half is objectui#10993's census row; this card is the attribute name, which is wrong for a plain string too.

## Measured (the dev's probe, through `SchemaRenderer`)

`{ type: 'element:text', aria: { ariaLabel: 'Plain name' } }` renders `aria-arialabel="Plain name"` and no `aria-label`.

## Why it matters

The spec declares an accessible-name channel on these elements, the registry accepts it, and the renderer silently drops it. An author (or an AI) who does the right thing for accessibility gets no effect and no error.

## Direction (for triage, not a ruling)

Map the spec's `AriaProps` keys to their attributes (`ariaLabel` → `aria-label`, `ariaDescribedBy` → `aria-describedby`, `role` → `role`), resolving an `I18nLabel` against the UI language, the way the other renderers' shared aria reader does (PR objectui#10855 names `resolveAriaProps` for the timeline root). Pin a plain string and a locale map on one element, with a lit control on a renderer that already applies the name.

## Dedupe

The 1016 most recently updated objectui issues and PRs, open and closed (down to #2231), were listed via REST and grepped locally:
- `ariaAttrs`: 1 hit, PR objectui#11050 (the source report);
- `aria-arialabel`: 1 hit, the same PR;
- `aria.ariaLabel` / `aria: { ariaLabel`: 4 hits, objectui#9945 and PR objectui#10609 (the `record:*` `aria.label` fold, a different reader), PR objectui#11041, PR objectui#11050;
- `AriaProps`: 4 hits, PR objectui#10855 (timeline root forwarding), objectui#9945, PR objectui#10609, PR objectui#11050;
- lit control `I18nLabel`: 22 hits; absent control `zzqq_never_written_token`: 0.

None carries the `element:*` attribute name.
